questions.question: Explain how 3D printing has changed the prototype development process in product design.

points.text: 3D printing allows designers to create physical prototypes directly from CAD files in hours rather than weeks; it enables iterative testing, reduces material waste compared to subtractive methods, and allows complex geometries that CNC cannot produce.

questions.question: Discuss the social and economic impacts of increasing automation in manufacturing.

points.text: Positive: increased productivity, consistent quality, reduced hazardous work for humans. Negative: job displacement, skills gap, initial investment costs, dependence on technology. A balanced answer considers both sides with specific examples.

questions.question: Evaluate how the Internet of Things could influence the design of a domestic kettle.

points.text: An IoT kettle could: be controlled remotely via smartphone, learn user habits for energy efficiency, alert users to limescale build-up via sensors, integrate with smart-home energy monitoring. Evaluation should weigh convenience against cost, privacy and reliability concerns.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response A company is considering replacing its traditional assembly line with robotic automation. Evaluate this decision, considering social, economic and environmental factors. <div class="

points.text: A grade 9 response will: define robotic automation and its capabilities; present social arguments (job losses vs new skilled roles, worker safety); economic arguments (high initial cost vs long-term savings, 24/7 operation, consistency); environmental arguments (energy use of robots vs human labour, reduced waste from errors); reach a justified conclusion considering the company's specific context — e.g. high-volume, precision manufacturing may justify automation whereas small-batch artisan production may not.
